messages.subject: Educator feedback on a free space-and-creature activity
messages.body:
Hi Blackrock Castle Observatory education team,

I’m Kevin, the founder of Mythical Void in Ireland. I’m reaching out because your education team develops space activities and helps teachers find useful classroom resources.

Mythical Void began as a father-and-son experiment with imagination and generative AI. We have now made a free four-page STEM Creature Lab for ages 9-14, families, clubs and classrooms. Learners begin with a credited real-space source, separate observation from fiction, design an organism for an impossible environment and write a prediction they could test. Younger designers are asked to work with an adult.

The activity is here: https://mythicalvoid.com/nasa-space-science/
The game and clearly labelled press material are here: https://mythicalvoid.com/press/

We do not collect work or personal information from children. The activity is independent and is not endorsed by NASA, ESA, ESERO, Research Ireland or BCO.

If you have time, I would value an adult educator’s view on whether the activity is useful and whether there is an appropriate route for suggesting external resources. If it is not a fit, no reply is needed.

Thanks,
Kevin
Mythical Void

messages.subject: Question about a free independent space-learning activity
messages.body:
Hi ESERO Ireland team,

I’m Kevin, the founder of Mythical Void in Ireland. Your teacher-support page offers classroom resources and support for bringing space into primary and post-primary learning, so I wanted to ask for the right adult review route.

Mythical Void is a free browser game that began as a father-and-son experiment with imagination and generative AI. We have made a free four-page STEM Creature Lab for ages 9-14, families, clubs and classrooms. Learners start with a credited real-space source, distinguish observation from a fictional idea, design an organism for an impossible environment and write a prediction they could test.

Activity: https://mythicalvoid.com/nasa-space-science/
Press and background: https://mythicalvoid.com/press/

We do not collect work or personal information from children. The activity is independent and is not endorsed by NASA, ESA, ESERO or Research Ireland.

Could you tell me whether there is a suitable route for an independent resource like this to be reviewed, or any changes an adult educator would recommend before it is shared more widely? If it is not relevant, no reply is needed.

Thanks,
Kevin
Mythical Void
